You Don't Need a Huge Following to Get PR Packages

Let's get one thing straight: brands are actively seeking small creators and micro influencers to send PR packages to in 2026. Why? Because micro influencers (1K–50K followers) consistently deliver higher engagement rates, more authentic content, and better ROI than mega influencers. If you've been searching for "brands that send PR to small influencers" or "PR packages for micro influencers," you're in the right place.

This guide covers everything: which brands send PR to small creators, how to position yourself to get noticed, and how to skip the waiting game entirely using Newcollab's creator marketplace.

Why Brands Send PR to Small Creators

The influencer marketing industry has shifted dramatically. Here's why brands now prefer small creators and micro influencers for PR packages:

  • Higher Engagement Rates: Micro influencers average 3–6% engagement compared to 1–2% for mega influencers. That means more comments, saves, and shares per post.
  • Authentic Content: Small creators produce content that feels genuine and relatable, not polished ads. This is exactly what consumers trust in 2026.
  • Cost-Effective: Sending a $50 PR package to 20 micro influencers generates more reach and trust than one $1,000 package to a macro influencer.
  • Niche Audiences: Small creators often have tight-knit, highly targeted communities — exactly what brands need for product launches.
  • Higher Conversion: Studies show micro influencer recommendations drive 22% more purchase decisions than celebrity endorsements.

- Jess K., Skincare Creator

What Are the Minimum Requirements?

This is the #1 question small creators ask: "How many followers do I need to get PR packages?" The honest answer: it depends on the brand, but it's lower than you think.

The key metrics brands actually look at:

  • Engagement Rate: Above 3% is the magic number for most brands
  • Content Quality: Clean, well-lit photos/videos in a consistent style
  • Niche Clarity: Brands want creators who speak to a specific audience (skincare, fitness, fashion, gaming, etc.)
  • Posting Consistency: At least 3 posts per week shows commitment

Even with under 1K followers, you can land PR packages if your content is high-quality and your engagement is strong. Browse brands on Newcollab's marketplace to find opportunities that match your niche.

Types of Brands That Send PR to Small Creators

Not all brands are equal when it comes to PR for small influencers. Here are the categories most likely to work with you:

Beauty & Skincare

The beauty industry is the most PR-friendly niche. Brands like ColourPop, e.l.f., CeraVe, The Ordinary, and emerging K-beauty brands actively seek micro influencers for product launches and reviews. Many have open PR application forms.

Clothing & Fashion

Fast fashion and streetwear brands are always looking for fresh faces. Shein, Princess Polly, PrettyLittleThing, Boohoo, and sustainable fashion brands regularly send PR to creators with as few as 1K followers. Check our clothing brand PR list for specific opportunities.

Food & Wellness

Supplement brands, snack companies, and wellness products love micro influencer content. Brands like HelloFresh, AG1, Bloom Nutrition, and smaller DTC brands are actively building creator networks.

Tech & Gaming

For streamers and tech creators, brands like Razer, Logitech, Secretlab, and indie game studios send PR packages and offer gaming sponsorships for small streamers.

How to Get PR With Less Followers

If you have fewer than 1K followers, here's how to still land PR packages:

  1. Lead With Content, Not Numbers: Create 3–5 sample "review-style" posts for products you already own. This shows brands exactly what they'd get by working with you.
  2. Use Newcollab: On Newcollab, you post content ideas and brands bid on them. Your follower count is secondary to your creative concepts.
  3. Target Small & Emerging Brands: Indie brands and new DTC companies are much more open to working with nano influencers. Search our brand directory to find them.
  4. Engage Authentically: Tag brands in genuine content (not begging for PR). Many brands scout creators who are already organically posting about their products.
  5. Build a Media Kit: Even with 500 followers, a professional media kit sets you apart from 90% of creators at your level.

Step-by-Step: Getting Your First PR Package

Follow this exact playbook to land your first PR package in 2026:

Step 1: Define Your Niche

Pick ONE niche (beauty, fashion, fitness, gaming, food, etc.) and make your entire profile about it. Brands want specialists, not generalists.

Step 2: Clean Up Your Profile

Professional bio, consistent aesthetic, clear contact info (email in bio), and a link-in-bio with your media kit. Your last 9 posts are your portfolio.

Step 3: Apply to Open PR Forms

Use our directory of 30+ brands with open PR application forms to apply directly. No guessing, no hunting for emails.

Step 4: Send Cold Pitches

For brands without open forms, use our copy-paste PR pitch templates to email them directly.

Step 5: Join Newcollab

Post your content ideas on Newcollab and let brands come to you. This is the most efficient way to get PR offers without chasing anyone.

  • K-Beauty Brands: Brands like COSRX, Laneige, and innisfree frequently send PR to small creators for product launches.

Fashion PR is competitive but very accessible for micro influencers who have a clear style identity:

  • Shein: The #SHEINfluencer program accepts creators with as few as 500 followers.
  • Princess Polly: Popular ambassador program for fashion and lifestyle creators.
  • PrettyLittleThing: Active PR list and collab email for fashion creators.
  • Boohoo: Works with a wide range of creators for styling content.
  • Gymshark: Scouts fitness and athleisure creators organically.

See our full clothing brand PR list for micro influencers.

How to Get Free PR Packages

All PR packages are free — that's the whole point. Brands send you products at no cost in exchange for content. Here's how to maximize your chances of getting free PR:

  • Don't Ask for Free Stuff: Frame it as a partnership, not a freebie request. Brands want creators who add value, not just collect products.
  • Show Your Value Proposition: Explain what content you'll create, where you'll post it, and who your audience is.
  • Be Professional: Use proper grammar, include your media kit, and follow up politely.
  • Start Small: Accept smaller brands first to build your portfolio of sponsored content. This makes pitching bigger brands much easier.
  • Use Multiple Channels: Apply through PR forms, send cold emails, AND use platforms like Newcollab simultaneously.

  • Get Discovered: Create your creator profile and let brands find you based on your niche and content style

The directory is updated regularly with new brands joining the platform. Sign up free to access the full directory and start connecting with brands.

Mistakes That Kill Your PR Chances

Avoid these common errors that get your applications rejected:

  • "Send me free stuff" energy: Never position PR as free products. It's a business partnership. Frame every outreach as value you bring to the brand.
  • No media kit: Brands receive hundreds of requests. A media kit makes you stand out immediately. Create yours with our free media kit template.
  • Generic pitches: "I love your brand" means nothing. Reference specific products, campaigns, or values that resonate with you.
  • Inconsistent content: If your last 9 posts span 5 different niches, brands won't know what to expect from a partnership.
  • Ignoring small brands: Everyone pitches Nike and Sephora. The fastest path to PR is partnering with emerging DTC brands that need micro influencer content.
  • Giving up after one rejection: PR is a numbers game. Apply to 10–20 brands per month and follow up on applications that don't get a response.

faq.question: How many followers do I need to get PR packages?
faq.answer: There's no universal minimum. Some brands work with creators who have as few as 500 followers, while others require 5K+. What matters more is your engagement rate (aim for 3%+), content quality, and niche alignment. Platforms like Newcollab have no follower minimums at all.

faq.question: Do brands really send PR to small influencers?
faq.answer: Yes. In 2026, micro influencer marketing is a $16+ billion industry. Brands actively prefer small creators because they deliver higher engagement, more authentic content, and better ROI. Beauty, fashion, and food brands are especially active in sending PR to creators with 1K–10K followers.

faq.question: What's the difference between PR packages and paid partnerships?
faq.answer: PR packages are gifted products sent for free in exchange for content (unboxing, reviews, etc.). Paid partnerships involve monetary compensation on top of or instead of free products. Many creator relationships start with PR and evolve into paid deals.

faq.question: How do I find brands that send PR to micro influencers?
faq.answer: Three main ways: (1) Use our directory of 30+ brands with open PR forms, (2) Browse Newcollab's brand directory to find brands actively seeking creators, (3) Search hashtags like #gifted, #PRpackage, and #brandpartner to see which brands are already working with small creators.

faq.question: Can I get PR packages with 0 followers?
faq.answer: It's very difficult with 0 followers, but not impossible. Focus on building at least 100–500 engaged followers first. In the meantime, create sample content and join Newcollab where brands evaluate your content ideas rather than follower count.
